rule: an overlay over URBAN_RULES 1.5.0 (itself the owner library 1.4.0 + the 1.5.0 overlay): an OWNER_APPROVED record replaces the record with the same rule_id or adds a new rule; the 1.4.0 and 1.5.0 files are never edited; frozen results keep the version they were computed with. engine/source/rule_store.py does not resolve 1.6.0 yet (VERSIONS 1.4.0 / 1.5.0, latest 1.5.0 unchanged): registering it is part of the integration path, so no method reads this file today except engine/source/stair_rule_calculator.py, which reads its one record directly

approval.source: owner main chat 2026-10-21, recorded in docs/agents/OWNER_RULE_STAIRS_2026-10-21.md on agents/control (the Arabic text governs; the owner's English version has the same content); answers S-1 .. S-3 the same day ("As you recommend")

records.rule_name: Stair riser / tread count and fit check from the floor height and the available length

en: two flights (U) with a mid landing

inputs.floor_height: m; finished floor level to finished floor level (S-3)
inputs.available_length: m; the horizontal length available for the stair

calculation_method: 1 risers = ceil(floor_height / max_riser), always rounded up
2 actual_riser = floor_height / risers: all risers equal, never a short leftover step
3 single straight flight: treads = risers - 1; required_length = treads x tread

4 two flights (U) with a mid landing: flight1 = ceil(risers / 2), flight2 = floor(risers / 2); treads per flight = its risers - 1 (total treads = risers - 2); required_length = (flight1 - 1) x tread + landing_depth
5 fit check: single flight when its required_length <= available_length; otherwise U when its required_length <= available_length; otherwise the warning 'space is not enough, needs at least X m'
7 the landing is never counted as a tread; the last riser lands on the landing or the upper floor
boq_outputs: risers, actual_riser, treads, stair type (single / U), required_length, fit result
tread cladding m2 = treads x tread x stair_width
riser cladding m2 = risers x visible_riser x stair_width, visible_riser = actual_riser - tread build-up (S-2; UP-STAIR-003, tread marble 0.030 m UP-STAIR-006)
tread pieces = treads; riser pieces = risers
landing m2 = landing_depth x (2 x stair_width), its own line

relations.UP-STAIR-002: S-1 answered DRAWING GOVERNS: when the drawing prints or draws the stair, its riser / tread count and geometry govern and this rule runs as a CHECK (a count mismatch, an actual riser above 0.16 m or a tread under 0.28 m is a flagged finding, never a silent change); when the stair is not drawn this rule is the owner-approved method and its quantities carry ASSUMED — OWNER-APPROVED with this record as the source. The 0.16 / 0.30 defaults are therefore never used on a drawn stair (UP-STAIR-002: typical values are diagnostic only)
relations.UP-STAIR-003: S-2 answered RISER LESS THE TREAD BUILD-UP: the riser finish area uses the visible riser, not the full actual_riser
relations.UP-STAIR-006: the tread build-up is the tread marble thickness, 0.030 m unless the drawing, specification or owner gives another
relations.UP-STAIR-009: the 0.155 - 0.165 m range stays a diagnostic sanity range; this rule's 0.16 m is a limit that raises a warning, never a measured riser of a drawn stair

open_points.question: precedence with UP-STAIR-002 when the drawing prints the stair
open_points.answer: the drawing governs; this rule checks it

open_points.question: riser cladding height: full actual_riser or actual_riser less the tread build-up
floor_height basis: finished floor to finished floor, or structural level to structural level

records.arithmetic: exact decimal arithmetic: 4.48 / 0.16 is exactly 28 risers (binary floating point gives 28.000000000000004 and ceil 29); limit comparisons carry a 1e-9 m tolerance
records.unit: nr | m | m2 (never summed across units, UP-STAIR-004)
records.unknown_behavior: STAIR_INPUT_NOT_ESTABLISHED (a missing floor height or width: no quantity); STAIR_DOES_NOT_FIT (every line HELD with the 'needs at least X m' warning); AVAILABLE_LENGTH_NOT_GIVEN (the type-dependent lines HELD, both types shown)
